requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. Stop retrying when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive transient failure.
2. That stop applies even when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass the one-minute point.
3. On stopping, fail with an error that names the attempt count and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.

**Unit test: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute]`**
- **Cut-off with simulated time.** It drives `ProviderBackoff::retry` with simulated time. Each `Wait` advances the clock, and the test asserts that no attempt starts after `start + 60s`. The loop ends in a `Stop`, and more than three attempts were made first, so backoff was really applied.
- **Boundary.** After a failure at `start`, a second failure at 58s still waits with a delay of at most 2s. This pins the "not more than a minute" side.
- **`Retry-After` boundary.** A `Retry-After` of `60` waits for exactly 60s. A `Retry-After` of `61` stops. This is the exact boundary, and it covers the clause "including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point". A `Retry-After` of `90` also stops at once.
- **Attempt count.** The message must contain `kept failing for a minute` and `after {attempts+1} attempts`.
- **Status and code.** The message must contain `HTTP 429 ThrottlingException`.
- **Partial information.** Three cases check the "when available" wording: status only (`HTTP 503`), code only (`ThrottlingException`) and a timeout with neither (`no response within ten minutes`).
- **First failure.** In each of those three cases, the first failure is made at `start + RETRY_LIMIT`, so the clock is measured from the first failure rather than from process start. A later failure at `start + RETRY_LIMIT*3` stops.
- **Permanent error.** A permanent 400 `ValidationException` stops with its own error, not the "kept failing" error.

**Integration test: `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_request_failing_for_a_minute_fails_the_assessment]`**
- It runs the whole assessment with a provider that always returns 503 `ServiceUnavailableException`, under paused tokio time.
- It asserts that elapsed time stays within `RETRY_LIMIT`.
- It asserts that more than three attempts were made.
- It asserts that the assessment error contains `after {attempts} attempts; last failure: HTTP 503 ServiceUnavailableException`, with the attempt count matching the provider's recorded requests.
- It asserts that the usage log's attempt counts are consistent, and that the last attempt is not marked retried.

**Gaps considered and ruled out**
- Resetting the clock after a success belongs to the parent `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`, not to this subject. `ProviderBackoff::retry` only records the first failure time, and a new backoff per completion request is what resets it.
- I found no obligation in this requirement text without a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST count toward the assessment totals under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
